column1: NUCRIPCE only applies when the user has a demand/activity. Eight drivers: Novelty, Urgency, Challenge, Routine, Interest, Passion, Collaboration, Exploration (two Cs by design: Challenge and Collaboration). Regulate is NOT in this list — see Tab 2 for Intervention domains. The user never sees this acronym in the UI.

column2: The activity is new, unfamiliar, different, or offers a new experience.
column3: Trying a new method, new topic, new environment, new creative activity.

column2: The activity has meaningful time pressure or a consequence for delay. Derived from Timeline (Tab 4), not user-labelled directly.
column3: Immediate task, same-day requirement, deadline-sensitive action.

column2: The activity requires problem-solving, sustained effort, complexity or stretch.
The activity is familiar, predictable, structured or low in decision cost.
The activity naturally captures attention, curiosity or engagement.
column3: Preferred topic, hobby, personally engaging task.

column2: The activity is strongly connected to personal meaning, values or enthusiasm.
column3: Purpose-led project, creative pursuit, cause-related activity.

column2: The activity inherently involves working with others, social participation, interaction or shared activity.
column3: Group work, volunteering, event, body doubling, meeting others.

column2: The activity involves inquiry, learning, information-seeking, experimentation, research or discovery.
column3: Learning a topic, comparing options, investigating a question.
